notes:
Summary: Enterprise logistics SaaS (fleet + TMS) evaluating Redwood Dedicated for real-time routing and customer-facing assistants. Primary driver: predictable per-hour throughput for peak loads (morning dispatch window) and tight 95th percentile latency targets for API responses used in routing decisions. Asking for committed GPU capacity plan that guarantees throughput and clear latency SLOs with fallback routing to lower-cost model variants during degradation.

POC findings / numbers:
- Baseline POC used 2xA10-equivalent nodes with continuous batching; sustained 1.2M tokens/day across routing+chat mix.
- Observed 95th P50 latency: routing model (gpt-like open model) ~220ms token latency, end-to-end (prompt+postproc) median 350ms on dedicated bench.
- Peak concurrency pattern: 700 concurrent sessions in 10:00-11:00 window; average request size 120 tokens; spiky arrival distribution.

Cost modeling discussion (what Nimbus cares about):
- Commit levels considered: 1) Minimal commit: 2 reserved GPUs; 2) Mid commit: 8 reserved GPUs; 3) High commit: 24 reserved GPUs + burst pool. Each scenario modeled with utilization (conservative/expected/optimistic).
- Utilization assumptions used in model: conservative 45% (allow headroom for peaks), expected 70%, optimistic 90% (if caching & batching aggressive).
- Unit economics: token-level cost derived from reserved capacity amortization + infra + ops. Example outputs from model: under mid-commit (8 GPUs) @70% util => marginal cost per 1k tokens ~$0.0065; under high-commit w/ aggressive caching @90% util => ~$0.0038/1k tokens. (Nimbus finance requested range & sensitivity table).
- Break-even analysis: shows committed pricing advantage vs hosted at sustained >550k tokens/day.

SLA / legal ask:
- 99.9% uptime for dedicated pool, 95th percentile latency SLO for routing calls <= 500ms (e2e), credits tiered by missed SLOs. Nimbus pushing for contractual right to capacity increases at fixed uplift.
- Data residency / KMS: must be able to bring keys + have audit logs for all inference requests.

Open technical questions:
- How Redwood plans reserved GPU placement across AZs to avoid correlated latency spikes during infra maintenance?
- Quantization profile impacts on route planning model accuracy — engineering wants default vs. custom quantization delta documented.
- Can Redwood supply token-level cost exporter for Nimbus billing alignment?

Commercial negotiation notes:
- Nimbus procurement team wants three-year commit with annual true-up; finance is comfortable with ARR range ~$400-900k but needs clearer unit economics by March 15.
- Competitive set: Anthropic / Vertex with managed endpoints — Nimbus sees Redwood advantage if we provide deterministic latency numbers + formal fallback policies.

Next actions for AE/SE/CSM:
- AE (Maya) to deliver full reserved-capacity spreadsheet (commit vs util vs unit-cost) + two GPU-sizing scenarios by 2026-03-15.
- SE (Diego) to run one more peak-simulation with KV cache enabled and collect 99th/95th token latencies (due 2026-03-12).
- CSM (Priya) to prep SLA draft template and coordinate with legal on data residency wording.

Notes style: shorthand, action-oriented. Quoted paraphrase from CTO: "If we can't get a predictable per-hour capacity plan with hard latency SLOs, procurement will default to managed cloud vendors."
